kept.excerpt: October 13, 2026 (Toronto, ON) - A new Liaison Strategies Toronto survey finds Mayor Olivia Chow leading Brad Bradford 51% to 46% among decided and leaning voters, with 3% choosing someone else. Renters favour Chow 57% to 40%, while homeowners favour Bradford 50% to 45%. Liaison surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Toronto residents from October 8 to October 9, 2026, using Interactive Voice Recording (IVR) technology. For the total sample, the margin of error is +/- 3.1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day primary polling release measures Chow’s narrow lead and identifies a housing-tenure division relevant to turnout sensitivity.

kept.excerpt: Chow still leads, but Bradford has cut her cushion to 3.5 points among decided voters. With 17 per cent undecided, Toronto’s race remains an open contest. CP24/CTV News Toronto/Nanos conducted a RDD dual frame (cell- and land-lines) hybrid random telephone and online survey of 757 residents of Toronto aged 18 years and over, from October 8th to October 10th, 2026. A random survey of 757 residents of Toronto is accurate ±3.6 percentage points, plus or minus, 19 times out of 20.
kept.relevance: An independent cutoff-day poll provides evidence that Chow’s advantage was small and substantial uncertainty remained among undecided voters.

kept.excerpt: Advance voting in Toronto’s 2026 municipal election ended on Sunday, October 11 at 7 p.m. 222,550 eligible voters voted during six days of advance voting. Advance voting turnout in recent elections: 2023 Mayoral by-election – 129,745 votes; 2022 Toronto municipal election – 115,911 votes. Election day is Monday, October 26 from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
kept.relevance: This official cutoff-day release confirms the election schedule and shows substantially higher advance participation than in the two preceding elections.

kept.excerpt: According to polling released by Forum Research Inc. after Tuesday night’s debate, Chow leads the mayoral race among decided and leaning voters with 46 per cent of support compared to Bradford, who follows with 42 per cent of support. The remaining results suggest that 12 per cent of respondents would vote for someone else. The poll was conducted on Oct. 6 through telephone surveys with 1,604 randomly selected Toronto residents over the age of 18. It carries a margin of error of 2.45 per cent, 19 times out of 20.
kept.relevance: This report supplies another polling firm's estimate following Alexander’s withdrawal and the first ensuing debate, supporting a competitive two-candidate race.

kept.excerpt: Toronto mayoral candidate Chris Alexander has pulled out of the race just weeks before election day. He made the announcement just a half hour before advance voting was set to begin in the city. Alexander has been polling a distant third in recent surveys behind incumbent Olivia Chow and Councillor Brad Bradford. In his announcement, he said he would not be endorsing any of the candidates and encouraged voters to read all the platforms and find the candidate that most aligns with you.
kept.relevance: The withdrawal of the leading third candidate changes the competitive field and makes the destination of his previous support important for assessing Chow’s prospects.

kept.excerpt: Half (47%) of Torontonians believe Mayor Olivia Chow deserves re-election, increasing 5 points since last year, and her approval rating is holding steady at six in ten (59%). Mayor Chow currently holds a 15-point lead over chief rival Brad Bradford in the horserace, but one quarter of likely voters remain undecided. These are the findings of an Ipsos survey conducted on behalf of the Toronto Star that was fielded between September 4 - 8, 2026. A total of n=1006 residents of Toronto aged 18+ participated in the survey which was fielded via the Ipsos’ panel.
kept.relevance: This earlier primary poll provides incumbent approval and re-election sentiment alongside a baseline against which the closer October polls can be assessed.

kept.excerpt: The Toronto City Clerk has certified 361 candidates for the 2026 municipal election. The official list of certified candidates is available on the Toronto Elections List of Candidates & Third Party Advertisers webpage. Election day is Monday, October 26 from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Advance voting will be available from Tuesday, October 6 to Sunday, October 11 from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
kept.relevance: This dated official release establishes the certified municipal election field and confirms the voting timetable before the forecasting cutoff.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-10-13, inclusive. Selected seven items with explicit publication dates on or before the cutoff; no prediction-market pages, betting odds, post-cutoff developments, or election outcome information are included. Dates and excerpts were verified against source text returned by web_search. Direct web_fetch failed because multiple fetch providers were registered; the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable and verification relied on indexed source text. The CityNews Forum-poll article was published October 6 and last updated October 7, both before the cutoff. The City of Toronto candidate-certification release was published August 24 and explicitly updated August 26, also before the cutoff. Poll populations and denominators differ; reported margins of error apply as described by each source and should not be interpreted as margins of error on candidate leads.
